summary_html: Agency **files a court petition** to open a **dependency** (or similar) case. Federal funding frameworks (IV-E/ASFA) link court oversight, reasonable-efforts findings, and permanency timelines to downstream actions.
authority_html:
- **ASFA / SSA Title IV-E** — court findings; timelines; permanency planning  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal review of court/agency performance measures

key_cases.case_name: C.C. v. Cabinet for Health & Family Services
key_cases.holding: The Court held that the Rules of Civil Procedure, including the discovery rules, apply to dependency, neglect, and abuse actions before the adjudication hearing, and it vacated the adjudication and disposition orders because the mother was denied pre-adjudication discovery.
key_cases.relevance: Once a petition is filed, the parent is entitled to interrogatories, document requests, and the other Civil Rule tools needed to defend the case.
key_cases.quote: a participant in a DNA action is entitled to the benefit of the Civil Rules, including the discovery provisions, so long as there is no conflict with the Juvenile Code

key_cases.case_name: Commonwealth, Cabinet for Health & Family Services ex rel. M.H. v. R.H.
key_cases.holding: The court held that issue preclusion did not bar the Cabinet from introducing evidence identifying a parent as the perpetrator of prior sexual abuse of the child's seven siblings, because the earlier court had not actually decided the perpetrator's identity and that identity is not material to a finding that a parent created a risk of sexual abuse; it vacated the dismissal and ordered an expedited adjudication.
key_cases.relevance: The decision preserves the Cabinet's ability to plead prior family history when opening a new dependency case on a later-born child.
key_cases.quote: The identity of the perpetrator of the abuse is not material to that finding.

key_cases.case_name: R.V. v. Commonwealth, Department for Health & Family Services
key_cases.holding: The court held, under the Due Process Clause and KRS 625.080(3) and 620.100(1), that indigent parents are entitled to counsel throughout the dependency proceedings and that parental rights may not be terminated unless the parent was represented at every critical stage; it reversed a termination where counsel had been relieved before the goal-change hearing.
key_cases.relevance: Counsel must be appointed for indigent parents in the dependency action itself, not only after a termination petition is filed.
key_cases.quote: Parents are entitled to a meaningful opportunity to be heard, including the right to consult with counsel, at goal change and permanency hearings

key_cases.case_name: Commonwealth, Cabinet for Health & Family Services v. C.V.
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed dismissal of the Cabinet's termination petition because the circuit court made no findings that would support termination, while agreeing with the Cabinet that a district-court change of the permanency goal from reunification to adoption is not a prerequisite to filing a termination petition.
key_cases.relevance: It holds that the Cabinet may file a termination petition without first obtaining a district-court permanency-goal change, clarifying the sequencing of agency filings.
key_cases.quote: Under KRS 625.090(3)(c), the court can make its own concurrent finding as to reasonable efforts
